author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page. Reachable by its address alone: no page links to it.
acceptance_criteria: opening the specialty directory at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, each by its stored name
each veterinarian holding a specialty is shown under it by first name followed by last name, for example "Helen Leary"
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
every specialty is shown on one page, with nothing to page through
the page carries navigation to owner search and to the veterinarian directory, and no page of the system carries an entry pointing to the specialty directory
edge case 1: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it
edge case 2: a veterinarian holding more than one specialty is shown under each of them
edge case 3: when the clinic knows no specialty at all, the page renders as an empty directory rather than failing
edge case 4: specialties are presented in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians within one specialty
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
a navigation entry or any link pointing to the specialty directory (deliberate for this slice; a follow-up request may add one)
showing veterinarians who hold no specialty
notes: REQ-SYS-001 is unchanged and holds on the new page: the page carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory. REQ-SYS-001 requires navigation ON every page, not an entry TO every page, so the no-entry decision needs no exception. REQ-LANG-002 applies: any new page wording is a message key present in every supported language, not text fixed into the page. Three open questions recorded in the PRD rather than blocking: a future visible entry point; which order the page lists in (narrowest reading taken: stable, unspecified); whether a specialty name is data or translatable wording.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is a second read surface over the vet feature package, built entirely from patterns already in force. One adjustment to durable memory is needed: the vet package gains a second persistence gateway. Edge case 1 (a specialty no veterinarian holds) cannot be served from Vet.getSpecialties(), because the ManyToMany runs one way only and an unheld Specialty is unreachable from any Vet; a SpecialtyRepository over the specialties table is therefore required, mirroring PetTypeRepository (system-design.md Contracts). Inverting the association is a projection, not a routing concern, so it lands in a small immutable value type (SpecialtyDirectoryEntry) rather than in the controller: architecture-principles.md Design Validation Checklist forbids adding a new rule to a web controller, and the value type is unit-testable with real Vet and Specialty objects and no MVC or JPA context. The route, template, and layout usage copy vetList exactly. system-design.md is updated with three Contracts rows and a note on the one-directional association; no ADR — every new type instantiates an In-force catalog pattern (Repository, Value object, Web controller), which the catalog admits without one.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is a third @GetMapping on VetController (per the prd-entry file targets; the vet package owns both concepts, so no second controller). The route takes no request parameter at all — no paging means no input to bind or validate.

VetController gains a SpecialtyRepository constructor argument alongside VetRepository; it reads specialties in name order and veterinarians via the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(), then hands both to the projection.

SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.directory(List<Specialty>, Collection<Vet>) is a pure static factory returning one entry per specialty, each carrying the veterinarians holding it. A veterinarian with no specialty is absent by construction — the inversion is driven from the specialty side, so no explicit exclusion is written.

The template renders through the existing layout fragment with an unmatched menu key: th:replace="~{fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body},'specialties')}". The fragment's menu items are fixed inside layout.html, so passing a key that matches none yields the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory (REQ-SYS-001) with no entry pointing at the new page. layout.html is not modified.

Wording: the heading and column labels reuse existing bundle keys — 'specialties', 'vets' (Veterinarians), 'name', 'none'. REQ-LANG-002 may need no new key at all; any key that is genuinely new goes into messages.properties and every messages_*.properties except messages_en, which I18nPropertiesSyncTest skips by fallback.

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository with an explicit ORDER BY name query — the shape SpecialtyRepository copies. Prefer VetRepository's narrower base (org.springframework.data.repository.Repository<Specialty, Integer>) over JpaRepository: minimal surface, and the page needs one read method.

page skeleton: layout fragment call with a menu key, #{...} for every label, ${...} for data. Veterinarian display name is ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}, which is exactly the "first last" form the acceptance criteria require.
getSpecialties() already sorts by name — the same Comparator convention the directory projection follows for its own ordering.

risks.risk: Annotating the new repository method @Cacheable("vets") to match VetRepository. Both would be no-argument methods sharing one cache, and Spring's default key for a no-argument method is SimpleKey.EMPTY — the specialty read would collide with VetRepository.findAll() in the same key space and return the wrong type.
risks.mitigation: Leave the specialty read path uncached. CacheConfiguration declares the 'vets' cache alone; adding a cache would mean touching system configuration and would inherit the un-evicted-cache open question (system-design.md Open Questions, item 5).

risks.risk: Adding a SpecialtyRepository constructor argument to VetController breaks the existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) slice: the context fails to load and showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList fail before any new test runs.
risks.mitigation: Supply the repository to the slice in the same change (the existing suite stubs VetRepository with @MockitoBean; testing-principles.md tolerates that usage for the collaborators already stubbed there). Both existing vet tests must still pass.

risks.risk: Treating "stable order" as whatever the database and collections return. VetRepository.findAll() returns an unordered Collection and Vet.specialties is a HashSet, so row order would vary across vendors and runs and edge case 4 would pass only by luck.
risks.mitigation: Fix the order in two places: ORDER BY name in the specialty query, and an explicit comparator in the projection for veterinarians within a specialty (last name, then first name, then id as tiebreaker). Both are then assertable without a database.

risks.risk: Literal page text. I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings walks every src/main HTML file and fails on text between tags that carries neither #{...} nor a th:text attribute — a hard-coded heading or column label fails the build.
risks.mitigation: Every label is #{key}; every datum is th:text="${...}". Run ./gradlew test before review, not just the vet tests.

risks.risk: Adding a navigation entry for the new page while wiring the layout. That silently breaks the acceptance criterion that no page carries an entry pointing to the specialty directory.
risks.mitigation: layout.html stays untouched; the page only passes a menu key that matches no existing item.

notes: Open questions, resolved to the narrowest reading and recorded rather than escalated. (1) Ordering: specialties by name, veterinarians within a specialty by last name then first name — deterministic and vocabulary-aligned, not arbitrary; if the product owner later wants a different order it changes one comparator. (2) Specialty names are data, not translatable wording: rendered as stored via th:text="${...}", which Thymeleaf escapes (system-design.md Threat Model, XSS row). No per-specialty bundle key is introduced, so a specialty added to the database needs no code or bundle change. (3) Empty directory (edge case 3): the page renders its heading and an empty list; no failure path exists because an empty query result is an empty list. If an empty-state line is added it needs a new key in every bundle. For an unheld specialty, the existing 'none' key matches how vetList.html marks a veterinarian with no specialty. NG-2 is unaffected: the slice adds one read method and no write path. Security posture unchanged — a parameterless read-only GET over data already public on /vets.html and /vets; no new trust boundary, no new dependency. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Durable memory written: docs/system-design.md — three Contracts rows (SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectoryEntry, VetController purpose and Implements), REQ-SPC-001 added to Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository, a note that the specialty association is one-directional and the projection is where its ordering is fixed, and a provenance clause scoping the survey banner to survey-era statements.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every data-derived value through th:text (specialty name, and the vet first/last name concatenation), never th:utext; the fragments/layout.html it composes with adds no unescaped sink for this page. A repository-wide grep for th:utext/unescaped across src/main/resources/templates found no instances, so the stored-name XSS class has no occurrence on the reviewed surface.

JPQL injection: SpecialtyRepository.findAll carries a constant @Query with no bind parameters, no string concatenation, no SpEL and no Sort/Pageable argument feeding ORDER BY, so there is no injectable fragment. VetController passes no user input into the query path at all.

Route exposure: GET /specialties.html takes no request parameter or path variable, performs only reads, and is annotated @Transactional(readOnly = true) at the repository. Consistent with NG-1 (no access control by design) for this reference sample.

Data leakage: the page discloses specialty names and vet first/last names, both already published unauthenticated by /vets.html and the /vets serialized route. The only newly reachable datum is a specialty no vet holds - non-sensitive lookup data and the explicit requirement. No identifiers, credentials, or PII beyond the existing vet directory are exposed.

Least privilege on the new repository: SpecialtyRepository extends the bare Repository marker and declares findAll alone, so no save/delete/findById surface is inherited and nothing is exposed through Spring Data REST.
No hardcoded secrets: the change set introduces no credential-, token-, key-, or password-shaped literal; the added Java, template, and test files carry only domain strings.

Supply chain: the change set touches no build file (build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties, gradle/ all unchanged), so it adds no dependency and no new CVE surface; the existing dependency set is unchanged by this slice.

Projection safety: SpecialtyDirectoryEntry matches the association on the store-assigned identity with an explicit null guard, and defensively copies the vets list in the compact constructor, so the rendered model cannot be mutated after construction.

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The literal route `/specialties.html` is a mechanism detail (Spring MVC view-resolution path), not a domain behavior — it fails the what/how litmus test (it would change under a different framework or language) and is exactly the class of routing detail `docs/system-design.md` exists to carry. The claim it is 'necessary because the page has no other entry point' does not hold: the same sentence already states the behavior fully without the literal path — 'reached by its own address... and by nothing else: no page carries an entry pointing to it' — and the Done-when bullet on this same requirement already says 'opened at its address' with no literal URL. The document's own established convention elsewhere avoids naming routes (e.g. the Known Defect note describes 'a second route' without naming it). The literal path adds no information the surrounding prose lacks and should be dropped, with the concrete path left to system-design.md's Contracts entry for VetController, which already documents the route.

The sentence 'SpecialtyDirectoryEntry ... is the only place in the vet package where ordering of that projection is fixed' is inaccurate. Verified against source: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() fixes specialty order via ORDER BY specialty.name (SpecialtyRepository.java:43), and SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.HOLDER_ORDER (SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.java:37-39) fixes only the order of veterinarians within one specialty. The directory's overall order is fixed in two places, not one; SpecialtyDirectoryEntry takes the specialty list in whatever order it is handed (directory(List<Specialty> specialties, ...) iterates the given order per its javadoc 'in the given order', SpecialtyDirectoryEntry.java:49) and does not fix specialty order itself.
findings.fix: Replace 'and is the only place in the vet package where ordering of that projection is fixed' with wording naming both fixed-ordering points, e.g. 'SpecialtyRepository fixes specialty order by name; SpecialtyDirectoryEntry separately fixes the order of veterinarians within one specialty.'

approved_aspects: Provenance banner amendments in prd.md and system-design.md are mutually consistent and correctly scope the survey-era disclaimer to pre-REQ-SPC-001 statements

New Contracts rows (SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectoryEntry, updated VetController/Vet/Specialty/VetRepository rows) stay at the source-pointer abstraction level with no field/parameter tables or transcribed constants
REQ-SPC-001 anchor, Done-when bullets, and edge-case list follow the PRD format and all edge cases from the prd-entry are covered
No new domain terms introduced; Specialty and Veterinarian are already defined in ubiquitous-language.md
Open Questions additions are appropriately scoped as open rather than smuggling in resolved mechanism
docs/system-design.md#contracts anchor referenced from prd.md resolves

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderEmptyWhenNoSpecialtyExists asserts content().string(containsString("Specialties")) — a bare string literal that happens to match the messages.properties value for the 'specialties' key. Per testing-principles.md Three-Tier Data Naming, this is a Tier 3 mystery value: nothing in the test names it as the expected heading, and a reader can't tell whether "Specialties" is meaningful (asserting page identity) or incidental. Swept the touched test files for the same pattern (grep -F -e '"Specialties"'); this is the only instance.
findings.fix: Extract a named constant (e.g. private static final String SPECIALTIES_HEADING = "Specialties";) at class or method scope, or assert against a value read from the same message bundle the template renders from, so the literal's role is explicit.

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryNavigationToOwnersAndVeterinarians only asserts the specialties page itself carries no href to /specialties.html — it does not check that any other existing page (vetList.html, owner pages, the layout menu) still lacks a link to the new page, which is the actual PRD acceptance criterion ('no page of the system carries an entry pointing to the specialty directory'). The design-block's mitigation (layout.html left untouched) makes this low risk today, but the test as written would not catch a future regression where a link is added elsewhere — e.g. directly in vetList.html rather than the shared layout fragment. Confirmed via grep that no template currently references specialties.html outside specialtyList.html itself.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryEntryTests: 8 unit tests, all pure/no I/O, real Vet/Specialty value objects (no mocks), one behavior asserted per test, BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming throughout, four-phase structure with blank-line separation and no phase comments, factory methods (createASpecialty/createAVet/createAnUnsavedSpecialty) wrap all construction, edge cases from the PRD (unheld specialty, multi-specialty holder, empty directory, stable ordering, unsaved/id-less specialty) each get a dedicated test with derived expectations (containsExactly against the actual input order)

VetControllerTests: the added @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository follows the pre-existing convention already established for VetRepository in the same @WebMvcTest slice — testing-principles.md explicitly tolerates continuing an existing mock-framework stub rather than introducing new debt; not a new violation

ClinicServiceTests: theSpecialtyReadShouldReturnEverySpecialtyInNameOrder is a genuine integration test against the real H2 fixture data via the real SpecialtyRepository — correctly placed at the integration tier per the brief's mocking policy (real I/O, no mocks)
All 8 PRD acceptance-criteria test_names are present and exercised across the unit and controller layers; ./gradlew test passes with no failures for the touched packages

Pyramid shift is consistent with the brief's guidance: the projection logic was lifted into a pure unit (SpecialtyDirectoryEntry) and given 8 unit tests, while the controller slice added only 5 thin wiring tests — moving the ratio toward the target rather than widening the web-layer-test gap

author: product-requirements-expert
answer: The narrowest reading is correct. "No page carries an entry pointing to the specialty directory" binds this change, not the whole template tree in perpetuity. The product owner's words were: "The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request." That is a statement about the scope of this request, not a standing invariant - and a system-wide assertion would actively fight the named follow-up, failing the moment the entry point everyone expects is added. The acceptance bullet overstated the criterion, so I tightened it: docs/prd.md now carries two bullets where there was one - the directory page carries navigation to owner search and to the veterinarian directory, and separately, this change adds no navigation entry and no link pointing to the specialty directory, on the directory page or on any other. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryNavigationToOwnersAndVeterinarians as written satisfies both halves for this slice; do not add a sweep over vetList.html, the owner pages, or the layout fragment. The absence of an entry point is deliberate scope, not a protected property. Related change in the same edit: the literal route was dropped from the REQ-SPC-001 prose and from the first acceptance criterion (doc-reviewer blocked finding at docs/prd.md:137, accepted). The behavior is unchanged - the page is reached by its address and nothing else - so no test needs to change on that account; the concrete path stays with VetController.
